I fixed the bug, and all 5 tests pass. That includes the new regression test.

`parse_price` in `inventory.py` now treats commas as thousands separators when the string is groups of exactly three digits after the first comma, with either a dot or a second comma group. So `"1,234.50"` gives `1234.5`, and `"$1,234,567.89"` and `"1,234,567"` also parse correctly. `"12,50"` still gives `12.5`, and `"12.50"` and `"$3"` are unchanged. I didn't touch `total_value`.

A lone `"1,234"` (one comma group, no dot) is still read as a European decimal comma, so it gives `1.234`. The issue's rule doesn't cover that case, so I left the old behaviour.

I added `test_thousands_separator` to `tests/test_inventory.py`. `unittest discover` only runs with `PYTHONPATH=.` because `tests/` isn't a package. I ran `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.
